script: A father, angry, shouted at his son: I give you to Death. So the boy, Nachiketa, went. Death wasn't home. The boy waited three days. To make up for it, Death offered him three wishes. For the last one, the boy asked: what happens when we die? Death offered him gold, horses, kingdoms instead. The boy said no. All of that ends. He wanted the one thing that doesn't. So Death gave him one word: om. One sound for everything, the part of everything that never ends. That's why Hindus start every prayer with om. Name the big thing first. Then ask for the small things.
